root_idea.summary: The root principally conveys cutting off, separation, or severance; a second lexical principle concerns binding or fastening.
root_idea.development: From separation develop abandonment, avoidance, mutual estrangement, and emigration. Related extensions include the midday pause in travel, disordered or foul speech, neglected vegetation, and terms for fastening or tethering.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Feminine plural active-participle occurrence; presented under the normalized singular participial citation form.

senses.definition: To cut off, abandon, leave, or avoid someone or something.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic constructions, the separation may concern bodily association, speech, or inward affection. It can describe leaving a person, avoiding association with people, or turning away from idolatry; the expression هَجْرًا جَمِيلًا specifies a gracious manner of avoidance.

senses.definition: To speak irrationally, foolishly, deliriously, or with foul and unseemly speech.
senses.usage_conditions: This is the speech-related Quranic use of the Form I verb and is distinct from physical or relational abandonment.

senses.definition: To emigrate or leave one place, land, or community for another.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic usage commonly concerns leaving a territory of unbelief or persecution for the believers, safety, or a place of refuge, and may be expressed as going forth to God. A broader religious interpretation extends the idea metaphorically to abandoning desires, blameworthy traits, and sins.
In the Quranic expression هَجْرًا جَمِيلًا, it is an avoidance carried out graciously; the separation may involve bodily association, speech, or the heart.

senses.definition: Forsaken, abandoned, or left without engagement.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic description of the Quran, this can mean that it has been abandoned through the heart, the tongue, or both.

senses.definition: Made into an object of irrational, false, or untrue speech.
senses.usage_conditions: A distinct Quranic interpretation takes the passive participle as referring to what people say about the Quran—speech that is irrational or untrue—rather than simply neglecting it.
The Quranic participle denotes a person who leaves a former homeland or community for another in the religiously significant sense associated with هَاجَرَ, including feminine plural مُهَاجِرَات.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go away, withdraw, or remove oneself to a distance.
To abstain from sexual intercourse while fasting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized fasting-related construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dream of or see someone or something in sleep; also, in some usage, to do so while talking deliriously.
To travel, go forth, or enter upon the time of the ẓahīrah or hājirah, the intense midday heat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may describe either journeying during that period or the day reaching it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut someone off from mutual friendly or loving intercourse; to forsake one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the transitive or reciprocal severance sense, distinct from the Quranic intransitive sense of emigrating.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To speak foul, evil, bad, abominable, or unseemly language; to talk excessively about what is improper.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form IV speech construction may also describe a person who has gone beyond his usual degree of such talk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mock, deride, scoff at, or ridicule someone with foul or unseemly speech.
To affect or pretend to be like the emigrants.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression can contrast genuine emigration with merely imitating emigrants in outward claim or manner.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut one another off from friendly or loving intercourse; to become mutually estranged.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Synonymous with mutual severance or قطع; this is a reciprocal construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To journey during the time of the intense midday heat.
Foul, evil, abominable, or unseemly speech; abusive or disgraceful words.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun also occurs in constructions for assailing someone with foul words or accusing them of disgraceful acts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The cutting off of friendly or loving intercourse; abandonment, desertion, or avoidance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This nominal branch concerns interpersonal severance rather than departure from one land to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Emigration: forsaking one's home, country, district, or land and taking up residence elsewhere.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can denote migration from a territory of unbelief to a territory of belief or safety, as well as ordinary removal from one place to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The Hijrah, the emigration of Muhammad from Mecca to Yathrib, later called Medina.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The technical historical term also occurs in الهِجْرَتَانِ, the two emigrations to Abyssinia and Medina, and in names for the Hijrah era.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Left, forsaken, relinquished, abandoned, neglected, or shunned.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival usage describing something or someone that has been left or avoided.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A custom, habit, wont, or habitual manner; also a person's customary speech or recurring saying.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related expressions هِجِّيرَى and إِهْجِيرَى denote a persistent customary practice or habitual preoccupation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who talks nonsense, foolishly, or deliriously.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Active-participle usage of the Form I speech branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The period of midday intense heat; the hājirah or noon interval.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may also be used elliptically for the noon prayer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who comes or arrives at the time of the midday heat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression for coming to one's family during the hājirah.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who journeys during the midday heat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A participial Form II usage connected with travel in the hājirah.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place to which one emigrates.
A rope used to fasten or tether a male breeding animal; by analogy, the string of a bow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The bowstring sense is a comparison with the tethering rope.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Extraordinary, unmatched, or excellent in quality.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A usage describing something as having no equal because of its distinction from other things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dry vegetation broken by grazing animals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended lexical usage associated with what the herder leaves behind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large basin or reservoir for water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is explained as something set apart or cut out for holding water.

cautions: The Quranic مَهْجُورًا has materially distinct classical interpretations: abandoned or neglected, and made the object of irrational or untrue speech; both are represented.
The feminine plural Quranic active participle مُهَاجِرَات is accounted for under the normalized singular citation form مُهَاجِر.
